title: How to Make a Short Film: 7 Steps, One Real Short
summary: Learn how to make a short film in 7 steps, from idea to final cut, with the real prompts, sketches and shots behind A Proper Introduction, made in Flick.
body_markdown:
### How long should a short film be?


Most short films run from 1 to 15 minutes, long enough for one character to change. The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences counts a film as short at 40 minutes or less, credits included.


### What are the steps to make a short film?


Find a small idea, write the script, design the characters, storyboard every shot, produce the shots, then edit with sound and music. With AI, producing the shots means generating a frame for each storyboard panel and animating it into a short clip.


### Can you make a short film with AI?


Yes. You write the story and direct each shot, and AI models generate the images, video clips, voices and music. In Flick, the character sheets, frames, clips and score of a short film all sit on one canvas, so you can trace every shot back to its prompt.


### How many shots are in a short film?


It depends on the pace and the length of each shot, so count them from your storyboard rather than a rule. With AI video, expect to generate several takes for each shot you keep, since the first take rarely gets the action right.


### How do you keep characters consistent in an AI short film?


Make a character sheet with front, side and back views for each character and use it as the reference image in every shot prompt. Describe the costume the same way each time and say which side faces the camera when the design is not symmetrical.


### Can I make a short film for free?


You can start a short film in Flick for free, with no credit card, and write the script, design characters and generate images on free credits. Video models such as Kling O3 Pro and Seedance 2.0 need the Standard plan or higher.


### Do you need a camera to make a short film?


Not with AI: every shot can be generated from a written prompt and a reference image. A phone camera is still useful for filming reference movement or real locations that you then mix with generated shots.
